title: OMP native HTML export
donor_inventory: Full per-task source attribution remains in #647 docs/plans/pr612-split/tasks.json, sections.json and net-diff.json. These are reference paths, not a cherry-pick; the donor generic native_action gateway is explicitly rejected and replaced by a feature-typed native HTML export consumer.
implementation: Render the live OMP session's persisted journal with OMP's own public export_html RPC on the already-owned session transport (correlated non-blocking begin/poll, never the blocking request lane, no second process/resume/lease/prompt). The adapter exclusively creates an owned staging file inside the OMP state root (sandbox-allowed), validates regular-file/exact-directory/exact-basename/16MiB, adopts the bytes verbatim into an anonymous GeneratedArtifact via an O_NOFOLLOW retained handle, and removes the owned staging on every terminal outcome including late post-timeout creation. Reuse task26 Files single-use grants, expiry, guest download budget, API completion composition and the shared client generated-artifact download pipeline. Native bytes are a download only, never rendered/sanitized/auto-opened; the UI shows an explicit nine-locale risk warning.
acceptance: Native export returns a downloadable file whose bytes match the native renderer output and receipt size/name; errors, cleanup, remote access and unsupported-version behavior are exercised. Active native execution keeps running with no extra input/writer/interruption. Old hosts receive no unsupported request. Owned staging is removed on success/failure/cancel/timeout/late-create/close; missing artifacts are not re-exported automatically. Real browser download of the native file is proven against an active official OMP turn.

results.result: Recovery run: 1 passed (3.3m), retries=0, official /usr/bin/omp with loopback OpenAI-compatible fixture. Actual browser download succeeded; receipt filename/size matched; decoded native journal preserved the seeded user message; risk warning visible; main turn stayed running during export and returned idle after fixture release. Recorded failure was a plaintext assertion against base64 journal data; corrected to semantic decoded-message verification. The recorded journal also proved the fixture had completed its supposed active turn; explicit hold/release now proves active execution.
